rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not terminate a covered tenancy without just cause (at-fault reasons or no-fault reasons such as owner move-in, demolition, or government order). No-fault evictions generally require relocation assistance to the tenant.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

unverifiable_exemptions: some non-profit homeless facilities or treatment centers
tenant has not lived in unit six months or original lease not expired

rules.coverage_conditions: Covers most residential properties in the City of LA not regulated by the RSO; applies once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease expired, whichever comes first. Can apply to buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and to a single single-family dwelling.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity/sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless/treatment facilities, some HACLA or government-owned properties.
rules.interaction: RSO units are covered by the RSO's own just-cause rules; JCO covers units not under the RSO. Supersedes state Civ. Code § 1946.2 for covered units.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.effective_date_note: Effective date not stated in document.
rules.conflict_note: State law (Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2) may overlap; local JCO is the stricter local rule.

rules.title: Los Angeles eviction for non-payment limited to rent above Fair Market Rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not evict a tenant for unpaid rent unless the amount owed exceeds the Fair Market Rent for the unit's bedroom size. This applies to all RSO and JCO units.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Eviction for Non-Payment of Rent (Fair Market Rent threshold)
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all RSO and JCO rental units.
rules.key_value: Rent owed must exceed Fair Market Rent for the bedroom size

rules.title: Los Angeles eviction notices must be filed with LAHD
rules.requirement: Every eviction notice served on a tenant must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service. Landlords must also post and provide a Notice of Right to Counsel.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Eviction Notice Filing Requirement (LAHD)
rules.quoted_span: All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all JCO and RSO rental properties.
rules.key_value: File within 3 business days of service

no_rule_findings.finding: The JCO itself does not regulate rent increases; for non-RSO units, rent increases are governed by state AB 1482 (Civ. Code § 1947.12).
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The JCO does not regulate rent increases, however, state law AB 1482, the California Tenant Protection Act of 2019

parsed.doc_summary: LAHD page on the Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance: covered units, at-fault and no-fault grounds, relocation assistance, the Fair Market Rent threshold for non-payment evictions, and the 3-day LAHD filing of eviction notices. It notes the JCO does not regulate rent increases (state AB 1482 does).
